title: Microburst-driven workload profiler and safe recommendation engine for batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a recommendation engine that detects microburst traffic patterns, profiles workload temporal characteristics, and proposes continuous batching parameters (batch size targets, horizon, cooldowns, and KV cache policies). The engine must generate conservative suggestions, support shadow/canary apply paths, and provide automated rollback if SLO regressions or cost regressions are detected.
motivation: Current autotuning focuses on average throughput but misses short, high-intensity microbursts that cause latency spikes or overbatching leading to tail latency regressions. A microburst-aware recommender will reduce per-token cost while preserving P95/P99 latency SLOs for latency-sensitive customers.
background: We have multiple autotune tickets (see dependencies) but lacked a concise profiler that encodes temporal burstiness, KV hit dynamics, and prefix reuse signals into safe heuristics. Existing profiling pipelines capture distributions but not burst-aware rolling-window metrics or rollback playbooks tied to canary results.
proposed_solution: Implement a lightweight microburst detector (exponential-weighted burst index) in telemetry pipeline to emit per-route burst score and burst window histograms.
Enhance workload profile schema to include: burst_score, burst_duration_percentiles, interarrival_entropy, prefix_reuse_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate, median_request_tokens, tail_request_tokens.

Build a recommendation engine that synthesizes profiles and outputs parameter set: target_batch_size, max_wait_ms, coalescing_horizon_seconds, cooldown_window_seconds, kv_policy (cache-size, ttl), and safety_margin_percent.
Score each recommendation by expected cost delta, estimated P95/P99 delta (simulated using trace-replay), and confidence band based on sampling density.
Provide UI + API payload for recommendations with rationale, simulated impact graphs, and rollback triggers.
Support a safe-apply flow: shadow apply -> canary (1-2% traffic) -> monitor (30m) -> gradual ramp with automated rollback on guardrail violations.
Integrate with existing rollout/orchestration system to execute canaries and attach automatic fallback to previous config.
Record every applied recommendation and canary result in a recommendation audit log for postmortem and ML feedback loop.
Expose simulation/what-if endpoints to let operators preview batch parameter effects on historical traces.
Provide an operator override annotation and emergency rollback button in Console.
Ship with a small set of pre-tuned heuristics for common workload archetypes (chat small tokens, chat long-context, embedding heavy, streaming short-responses).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): telemetry changes and profile schema rollout in staging; collector emits burst metrics for 10 routes.
Phase 2 (3 weeks): offline recommendation engine prototype; run recommendations in shadow mode and generate simulated impact reports for sampled traffic traces.
Phase 3 (2 weeks): integrate safe-apply orchestration with canary pipeline; perform 1% traffic canaries for non-critical tenants.
Phase 4 (2 weeks): expand to 25% traffic for pilot customers with manual review; collect metrics and tune heuristics.
Phase 5 (ongoing): full auto-recommendation opt-in for eligible customers with automated rollback and ML feedback loop.

Rollback plan: immediate rollback on any of the guardrail violations (detailed below). Manual rollback button available in Console; automated rollback reverts to last known-good config and notifies SRE/owner.
Post-release: 30-day evaluation window with weekly quality/cost reports and an adjustment cycle.
Owner: Marcus Nguyen; SRE support: Elena Rossi; Product: Tomás García; Design: Priya Menon.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry emits burst_score and burst histogram for all sampled routes in staging and production shadow runs.
Recommendation API returns parameter set with expected cost delta and confidence score for >90% of sampled routes.
Shadow apply simulation must not change live routing and must produce replayed latency/cost delta within 10% of canary results.
Canary mechanism can perform 1% traffic apply and collect guardrail signals automatically.
Automated rollback triggers on guardrail violations and successfully reverts config in under 5 minutes with an audit entry.
Operator Console surfaces recommendations with rationale and rollback control and logs operator overrides.
Initial pilot shows >=8% average per-token cost reduction on burst-prone workloads without exceeding P95 SLO by more than 5%.
End-to-end tests simulate microburst traffic and verify no more than 1.5x increase in error rate or P99 during canary compared to baseline.
Documentation and runbook published for SRE/solutions engineers.
telemetry_signals: Burst score (EWMA-based) and burst window percentiles
Batch size distribution and realized per-batch token count
KV cache hit/miss rate and TTL utilization
Cost per 1k tokens and instantaneous throughput
Queueing time vs service time breakdown
guardrails_and_triggers: P95 increased by >10% relative to baseline during canary -> immediate rollback
Error rate increases by absolute 0.5 percentage points over baseline -> immediate rollback
Percentile-cost-per-token increases >15% without latency improvements -> abort and rollback
GPU utilization spike above safe threshold (customer-specific) combined with latency degradation -> rollback
KV hit rate drop >20% resulting in increased CPU usage -> rollback and revert cache policy
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overfitting heuristics to sampled tenants. Mitigation: conservative safety_margin_percent and manual review for first 6 weeks.

Risk: False positives in microburst detector causing unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: require sustained guardrail violation (2 consecutive windows) before automated rollback, and expose manual override.
Risk: Increased operational complexity. Mitigation: consolidate recommendations into digestible UI with clear rationale and one-click revert.
Risk: Simulation mismatch vs real traffic. Mitigation: validate simulations with multiple replay datasets and shadow runs before canary.
Risk: Customer-facing regressions for high-SLO tenants. Mitigation: initial opt-in pilot, per-tenant opt-out flag, and tenant-level safe-mode that disables auto-apply.
updates: 2025-01-23: Spike complete for burst index calculation; prototype EWMA burst score implemented in telemetry collector (staging only).
2025-01-30: Offline replay harness extended to include burst window slicing; initial simulations show conservative batch size increase yields 6-9% token cost savings on median burst routes.
2025-02-06: Recommendation schema reviewed with Product and SRE. Added cooldown_window_seconds and confidence band fields per feedback from SRE.
2025-02-12: Shadow-run executed for 12 routes in staging for 48h. No guardrail violations observed; deltas in simulation vs shadow within expected variance (±7%).
2025-02-15: Canary orchestration work merged to internal rollout service (PR #112). Preparing 1% traffic pilots with two pilot tenants next week.
2025-02-18: Pilot canary started for tenant-redwood-pilot1; monitoring dashboard linked.
notes_for_reviewers: Reviewers: please focus on the guardrail thresholds and simulation assumptions — especially the sustained-violation requirement for automated rollback. Look at the conservatism of safety_margin_percent and whether per-tenant profiling should adjust margins automatically.
